1. Call to Order
   Mayor Brown called the meeting to order.

2. Declarations of Conflict of Interest

   Street.

3. Approval of Agenda
   It was requested that the Protective & Emergency Services Committee report be moved to the beginning of
   the discussion items. Moved and seconded that the agenda be approved as amended. Carried.

Regular Meeting of Council                         Page 2 of 7                                        December 9, 2025


   4. Adoption of Previous Draft Minutes of Council
      Moved by Councillor Ramsay and seconded by Deputy Mayor Jankov that the draft minutes of the following
      open meetings of Council be adopted.

                  Regular Meeting – November 12, 2025
                  Special Meetings – November 25, 2025
                                                                                                             CARRIED

   5. Business Arising out of the Minutes

       Regular Meeting of Council (November 12, 2025)
        CUPE 830 Collective Agreement - the City Solicitor indicated the Mayor and CAO are the signing authorities
         for the City. She further indicated the agreement is now with the Union for additional comment and
         anticipates execution of the document in the near future.

        Monument Installation Policy - it was confirmed that staff are proceeding with the development of a draft
         policy.

       Special Meeting of Council (November 25, 2025)
        Fire Underwriter’s Survey - It was reiterated that the item was held in a Closed Session as staff continue
          to look at suitable property for a third fire station and if discussions were held in public, it would likely
          prejudice a municipality’s ability to carry out its negotiation.

   6. Council Inquiries to be taken Under Consideration
      No inquiries raised.

   7. REPORTS OF COMMITTEES/RESOLUTIONS/BYLAW READINGS

       7.1    Protective & Emergency Services – Councillor Julie McCabe, Chair
       Councillor McCabe indicated her Committee report was included in the weekend package.

       Moved by Councillor Julie McCabe
       Seconded by Councillor Kevin Ramsay

       RESOLVED:
            That the City enters into an agreement with the Federal Department of Public Safety and
            Emergency Preparedness in relation to the Assault-Style Firearms Compensation Program,

               And that Mayor and CAO are hereby authorized to execute standard contracts and agreements
               in implement this resolution.

       Councillor McCabe indicated this is a federal program; RCMP in Charlottetown are under federal
       jurisdiction and it seems like a duplication of service. Council believes there are other priorities
       Charlottetown Police could focus on including reinstating school resource officers in city high schools. It
       was noted that only two (2) other jurisdictions have participated in the program thus far – Cape Breton
       and Winnipeg.
                                                                                                         LOST 10-0

Regular Meeting of Council                    Page 3 of 7                                December 9, 2025


       Moved by Councillor Julie McCabe
       Seconded by Councillor Kevin Ramsay

       RESOLVED:
            That the City enters into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Prince Edward Island
            Ground Search and Rescue (GSAR)Organization to continue the partnership between
            Charlottetown Police Services and GSAR,

               And that Mayor and CAO are hereby authorized to execute standard contracts and agreements
               in implement this resolution.
                                                                                           CARRIED 10-0

       1st Reading to Amend the Enforcement and Summary Proceedings Bylaw - Amend the City of
       Charlottetown Enforcement and Summary Proceedings Bylaw (#2024-ESP-01) to improve alignment
       with the Municipal Government Act of PEI Sections 236 and 238, strengthen enforcement provisions,
       clarify summary conviction offense, and expand on proceedings that can be processed through the
       Justice of Peace vs. Provincial Court judge.

       Moved by Councillor Julie McCabe
       Seconded by Councillor Kevin Ramsay

       RESOLVED:
            That the bylaw to amend the “CITY OF CHARLOTTETOWN ENFORCEMENT AND SUMMARY
            PROCEEDINGS BYLAW #2024-ESP-01" be read a first time.
                                                                               CARRIED 10-0

       Moved by Councillor Julie McCabe
       Seconded by Councillor Kevin Ramsay

       RESOLVED:
            That the bylaw now be approved as a City Bylaw and that it be entitled the “CITY OF
            CHARLOTTETOWN ENFORCEMENT AND SUMMARY PROCEEDINGS BYLAW #2024-ESP-01" and
            that it be read a second time at the next public meeting of Council.
                                                                                           CARRIED 10-0

       1st Reading to Repeal Emergency Measures Bylaw and Replace with the Emergency
       Management Bylaw - Repeal the Emergency Measures Bylaw adopted July 12, 1999 and replace with
       the Emergency Management Bylaw, #2025-EM-01. The purpose of the Emergency Management Bylaw
       is to establish an emergency management program to outline organizational structure and procedures
       for the City of Charlottetown to effectively manage emergencies and disasters.

       Moved by Councillor Julie McCabe
       Seconded by Councillor Kevin Ramsay

       RESOLVED:
            That the “CITY OF CHARLOTTETOWN EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT BYLAW, #2025-EM-01", be
            read a first time.
                                                                           CARRIED 10-0

Regular Meeting of Council                       Page 4 of 7                                    December 9, 2025


       Moved by Councillor Julie McCabe
       Seconded by Councillor Kevin Ramsay

       RESOLVED:
            That the bylaw now be approved as a City Bylaw and that it be entitled the “CITY OF
            CHARLOTTETOWN EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT BYLAW #2025-EM-01" and that it be read a
            second time at the next public meeting of Council.
                                                                                           CARRIED 10-0

       In response to an update request regarding the unsightly property at 31 Kirkwood Drive, Councillor
       McCabe referred the matter to the Deputy Fire Chief, who advised that the property is classified as
       vacant. Additional information, including timelines, will be presented at the next Committee meeting.

       7.2     Planning & Heritage – Deputy Mayor Alanna Jankov, Chair
       Deputy Mayor Jankov indicated her Committee report was included in the weekend package. Planning
       resolution #5 re: 1B West Street was moved to the first of the Committee report.

       Moved by Deputy Mayor Alanna Jankov
       Seconded by Councillor Julie McCabe

       RESOLVED:
            That the Heritage Board’s request, which is contrary to the Heritage Officer’s recommendation
            pursuant to section 3.4 of the Heritage Preservation Bylaw, that a 45-calendar-day Temporary
            Designation not be placed on 1B West Street (PID# 365833), be approved.

       Deputy Mayor Jankov spoke to the item noting that Staff’s recommendation is to place a 45-day
       temporary designation on 1B West Street but felt as the City’s advisory body on heritage matters, the
       Heritage Board’s review and recommendation were seen as sufficient and procedurally appropriate.
       Several Councillors indicated that the home is located within the City’s 500 Lot Area, which already
       carries design controls and heritage-related oversight and the property owner stated they did not want
       a temporary heritage designation.

       The Deputy Mayor then moved to amend the motion as follows:

       Moved by Deputy Mayor Alanna Jankov
       Seconded by Councillor Julie McCabe

       RESOLVED:
            That the Heritage Board’s recommendation that a 45-calendar-day Temporary Designation
            not be placed on 1B West Street (PID# 365833), be approved.
                                                                                        CARRIED 9-1
                                                                             Councillor Beck opposed

       • Councillor McCabe left the meeting at 6:12 PM.

       • Council took a brief recess at 6:13 PM and returned at 6:21 PM.

       • Councillor Muttart left the room for the following resolution as he was in conflict.
